title: The Thief and the Merchant

full_text:
In the city of Isfahan lived an affluent silk merchant named Kamal, celebrated for his tranquil temperament and generous charity. One night, while reading ledgers late in his inner counting-house, Kamal heard a soft rustling sound from the ceiling rafters.

Looking up calmly, he saw a young thief descending by a silk cord, clutching an iron pry-bar. The thief slipped into the room, only to find the master sitting at his desk, watching him with gentle curiosity.

The trapped burglar turned pale, raised his pry-bar, and snarled: 'Do not cry out for the watch, old man, or I shall strike you down!'

Kamal did not flinch. He set down his reed pen, gestured toward a cushioned stool, and said in a soothing voice: 'Peace be upon you, young friend. Sit down and catch your breath; climbing down rafters in the dark is weary work. It is cold tonight; let me pour you a cup of hot spiced tea.'

The thief stood dumbfounded, his weapon lowering in confusion. No victim had ever offered him tea before.

Kamal poured the hot beverage, handed the youth a bowl of sweet almonds, and asked gently: 'What bitter distress has forced a strong, intelligent young man like you to risk his life and honor in the dark alleys?'

The youth hung his head in shame, weeping: 'My father was an honest weaver who died leaving great debts. My mother and little sisters are starving, and no merchant will give employment to a penniless lad.'

Kamal opened his iron cash-box, counted out one hundred silver dirhams, and placed them in the youth’s hands: 'Take this sum to pay your father’s debts and buy flour for your mother. Tomorrow morning at sunrise, come to my silk shop in the central bazaar; I need a trustworthy assistant to manage my caravans.'

The young man fell to the floor, kissing Kamal’s sandals, swearing to renounce crime forever. He served the merchant with heroic fidelity for thirty years, eventually inheriting the business and continuing the tradition of turning compassion into honest opportunity.
moral: Repaying theft with kindness and practical opportunity converts a criminal into a lifelong ally.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Thief and the Merchant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
